problem.cause: The adapter reserved future slots before client/watcher setup and did not revalidate overdue reservations. Time-consuming setup could consume the spacing before transport entry.

changes: Finish client/watcher setup and the explicit durable worker-budget refresh before final adapter admission.
Recompute eligibility from actual admission time under a short lock after every bounded sleep; release the lock before sleeping and response work.
Use a pre-callback monotonic anchor for a conservative worker-budget deadline and only local elapsed-time subtraction on the successful path after admission.
On exhausted snapshot, never dispatch. Preserve an authoritative stop exception when available; otherwise use existing OperationTimedOut so the collector preserves provider health.

Replace client-construction and budget-call-count test assumptions with transport-dispatch and response-state assertions. Preserve the original 0.075-second threshold and concurrency-two overlap assertion.
Use module-local clocks in all new regressions and in the adjusted pacing cancellation test.

boundary.guarantee: Pacing of final adapter admissions before transport entry.
boundary.limits: This is not a formal wire-arrival guarantee under arbitrary OS scheduling. SourceTransport retains intentional durable cancellation checks during DNS, connect, TLS, reads and writes.
boundary.conservative_budget: Time spent obtaining the authoritative remaining budget is charged from the pre-callback anchor, so the derived timeout can be shorter than the worker's actual remaining deadline. It never adds that callback time to the budget.
boundary.exception_contract: workers.operations.OperationTimedOut; services/discovery/sources/collect.py restores prior health/failure metadata for local stop categories. The failure-only lazy import follows the collector's existing convention and avoids a new module-load dependency.
